title: Jeff Bezos Buys a Piece of Liverpool Football Club
partialText: It is the first known investment by Mr. Bezos, one of the world’s richest men, into a sports team.

title: July Retail Sales Notch Biggest Drop in Over a Year
partialText: The data for July showed the biggest drop in more than a year, as American households face the economic strains brought on by persistent inflation

title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
partialText: Investment gains at Alphabet and Amazon reveal a new way in which technology companies’ fortunes are increasingly linked.

title: Why Japan Is Struggling to Stop the Yen’s Decline
partialText: The currency has resumed its slide, eroding gains after the U.S. Treasury intervened to prop it up, as concerns mount about the direction of the country’s spending.

title: The Markets Have Been on a Roll. Is It Time to Hedge Your Bets?
partialText: The S&P 500 is in position for a rare fourth year of consecutive annual gains. Risks are rising, our columnist says, yet Wall Street is doubling down.

title: Robinhood Bets Again on a Public Venture Capital Fund
partialText: The trading platform raised $200 million for a second publicly traded vehicle to let ordinary investors buy into privately held start-ups.

title: New Yorkers Can’t Stop Lining Up for This Sushi
partialText: At a proliferating number of stores, discounts on sushi and other items are offered after 8 p.m. To get the best meals, you have to be there early.

title: A Silicon Valley Dirt Farmer Hangs Up His Shears
partialText: Andy Mariani grows exotic and ethereally delicious stone fruit in the shadow of tech giants. But at age 80, it’s time to give up the land.

title: How Pennsylvania Got Hooked on Games That Look a Lot Like Slot Machines
partialText: A legal loophole kept “skill games” from being considered gambling. Now lawmakers are trying to save them from a court ruling.

title: Kalshi Ordered to Cease Most Operations in Washington State
partialText: In a preliminary injunction, a state judge barred the prediction market from allowing residents to place bets on the bulk of its offerings.

title: Salvage Company Hoping to Sell Titanic Artifacts Challenges Court’s Role
partialText: A Virginia federal court has awarded the company the rights to collect, but not sell, items from the shipwreck. But the company says its earliest retrievals are governed by a French court.

title: Flock Announces Privacy Updates to Its Car-Tracking Cameras
partialText: Critics say the measures are “public relations” and leave room for continued misuse.

title: Alfonso Fanjul Jr., Cuban American Sugar Baron, Dies at 89
partialText: With his brother, he presided over a family empire that includes the world’s largest cane sugar refiner and the Domino and C&H brands.

title: In a Chinese Leader’s Death, Mourning for a More Hopeful Time
partialText: Tributes for former Premier Zhu Rongji reflect nostalgia for an era when China was opening to the world and the future seemed more prosperous and hopeful.

title: How Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner’s Bromance Led Them to Lakers
partialText: Bob Iger, the former chief executive of Disney, and Josh Kushner, the venture capitalist, are buying the Los Angeles Lakers. Their wives set them up.

title: Inside the $12.5 Billion Deal for the Lakers
partialText: The transaction, hashed out last weekend, reflects the huge profit potential of major sports franchises.

title: What We Know About Taylor Farms’ Food Recalls
partialText: Just weeks after the company recalled lettuce and other produce suspected of being tainted by the cyclosporiasis parasite, it recalled jalapeños linked to a salmonella outbreak.

title: America Wants to Make Its Own Humanoid Robots. That Won’t Be Easy.
partialText: China already manufactures humanoid robots by the thousands. A new generation of U.S. start-ups is betting that there is still time to compete.

title: The Golden Age of Mexican Food Is Here. And It’s Complicated.
partialText: Even at a time of anti-immigration politics, there has never been a richer variety of Mexican restaurants in the United States.

title: Who Is Joshua Kushner, the New Lakers Co-Owner?
partialText: The brother of Jared Kushner is an influential venture capitalist with big bets on A.I. and health insurance.

title: Treasury Scales Back Scrutiny of U.S. Shell Companies
partialText: The Trump administration will not enforce reporting requirements of the 2021 Corporate Transparency Act, which was intended to crack down on money laundering.

title: Forbes Fired Top Editor After Discovering He Received Secret $6 Million Payment
partialText: Randall Lane, the magazine’s chief content officer, received the money from the founder of Shook Research, which has worked with Forbes on content about wealth advisers.

title: Prediction Firms Are Flagging Insider Traders. Many Will Not Face Charges.
partialText: The agency that polices the industry does not have the staffing, the legal tools or the will to broadly crack down on wagers that are easily manipulated, experts say.

title: Ted Decker, CEO of Home Depot, Is Taking Medical Leave
partialText: Ted Decker is expected to return in a few months, and two executives have been appointed to oversee his duties in the interim.

title: Gulf Oil Giants Are Spending Billions to Build Ways Around Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Even if a cease-fire materializes, Gulf exporters recognize that relying strictly on the Strait of Hormuz is a risk they can no longer take.

title: Consumer Debt Data Shows ‘Overall’ Health Amid Persisting Divides
partialText: Homeowners with low fixed-rate mortgages lead a resilient picture of the economy. But many consumers are frustrated with declining real wages and other loans.

title: Will Paramount’s Brinkmanship Work?
partialText: The media company’s leader, David Ellison, is threatening to pull the company out of California in the face of a lawsuit by states seeking to block its big deal.

title: Thrive Holdings, A.I.-Focused Buyer of Service Firms, Raises $2 Billion
partialText: The company, Thrive Holdings, acquires businesses to infuse them with artificial intelligence and drew interest from backers like SoftBank.

title: Benign Inflation Data Offers Reprieve to Fed as It Weighs Rate Increase
partialText: The latest Consumer Price Index report helped to reinforce the patient approach adopted by many officials at the Federal Reserve about raising rates, but it has not resolved the debate altogether.

title: The labor market slowed as employers grew wary of hiring.
July CPI Report Is Expected to Show Falling Energy Prices
partialText: The war with Iran injected volatility into the oil and gas market, with prices rising and falling in concert with the conflict.

title: Homeowners tight on cash are tapping into their homes’ equity.
Inflation Eased Slightly in July, but Prices Remain Elevated as War Drags On
partialText: Though energy prices fell last month after their spring surge, other factors pushed up costs as the Fed considers raising interest rates.

title: Heat Kills Hundreds of Workers Each Year. A Postal Carrier Was One.
partialText: About half a dozen states explicitly protect workers from excessive heat. And some others, like Texas, prevent local governments from passing their own laws.

title: David Ellison Floats Hollywood Exit as States Threaten His Warner Bros. Deal
partialText: Mr. Ellison told Paramount executives that he was considering pulling the company out of California amid a lawsuit brought by state attorneys general.

title: Judge Awards $250,000 to Musician Who Fled Trump-Led Kennedy Center Gig
partialText: The center had sued Chuck Redd when he canceled a free concert last year, citing the addition of the Trump name to the venue. But a judge dismissed the case.

title: Frenzy for Solar Eclipse Glasses Takes Over London
partialText: Ahead of Wednesday’s rare cosmic event, thousands of people in London are searching for protective eyewear, as prices surge and stocks sell out.

title: G.M.’s ‘Car Guy’ Talks Electrics, China and Nepotism
partialText: Mark Reuss became the automaker’s president seven years ago, ascending to a role his father was fired from decades before. We got the chance to speak with him.

title: Robots That Walk and Talk Are Coming to Car Factories
partialText: But experts warn they may not deliver the gains in efficiency that proponents claim.

title: Ari Emanuel’s Company to Acquire 7 Broadway Theaters and 10 in the West End
partialText: The purchase of ATG Entertainment, which operates dozens of venues worldwide, will require regulatory approval.

title: The Perils of Wall St.’s Race to Pour Billions More Into A.I.
partialText: Investors including BlackRock have committed an eye-popping amount to lend to the artificial intelligence industry. That enthusiasm isn’t shared by everyone.

title: Oil Prices Touch $90 a Barrel Over U.S.-Iran Stalemate
partialText: The stalemate over the Iran war hardened and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz continued to dwindle.

title: Heat, Fire, Smoke and Storms Are Wreaking Havoc on the Economy
partialText: Businesses are reckoning with the financial toll of this year’s brutal climate shocks.

title: How Social Media Sparked a Refugee Crisis Between Spain and Morocco
partialText: A wave of disinformation online contributed to a surge of migrants in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta who were trying to reach Europe, resulting in about 90 deaths.

title: Should You Be Dating While Unemployed?
partialText: If you’re single and unemployed, it may make sense to prioritize job hunting. But that doesn’t have to mean putting your life on pause.

title: As Credit Card Debt Mounts, Home Becomes a Piggy Bank
partialText: A rise in home equity to record levels has led many Americans to refinance their mortgages to pay their bills.

title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
partialText: Six giant investment firms announced a $500 billion effort to raise money for customers of Nvidia to pay for computing power.

title: Traffic to Trump’s Truth Social Falls Sharply This Summer
partialText: President Trump’s social media platform has had double-digit declines in visitors in June and July, according to estimates from a widely cited online tracking firm.

title: Trump Shrugs Off A.I. and Data Center Concerns as Voters Grow Anxious
partialText: The president and his top aides have been especially bullish about data centers, despite national blowback against the facilities.
